seo.name: Matheapolis
seo._name: The wordmark on its own, for og:site_name (src/layouts/Layout.astro). The club was the Minneapolis Math Book Club until 2026-11-07, when the operator rebranded it: "I want the focus on the people and the ideas more than the book. the book is more an inspiration". A site_name that carries a descriptor makes two claims in the field a platform uses to label its source, so the descriptor lives in "title" instead. Do not use this slot to rename the Meetup group or the Mobilizon group - those are other organisations' records, listed in design/grill/copy-options.mjs as ORG_OF_RECORD.
seo.title: Matheapolis - a Twin Cities math club
seo._title: Was 'Join the Minneapolis Math Book Club | Math Book Discussions' — an imperative and a keyword phrase, in the voice of a listing rather than the club. og:title and twitter:title read this slot, and it is what a search result bolds, so it is the wordmark plus the descriptor the operator ruled on 2026-11-07 ("A Twin Cities math club"). It does NOT carry the old name: the continuity line is in the hero copy, where a person reads it, and the old apex keeps serving rather than 404ing, which is what actually preserves six years of links (D112's locator rule, applied to metadata).
seo.description: A math club in the Twin Cities. We work through papers, proofs, proof assistants and puzzles together, around a table in a coffee shop or a brewery. Dates and sign-up on Meetup; the discussion runs in the chat.
seo._description: Was 'Connect with fellow math lovers in our vibrant reading community. Monthly meetups, engaging discussions, and diverse book selections in Minneapolis, MN.' — 'vibrant', 'engaging' and 'diverse' are unsourced adjectives, and 'diverse book selections' describes a service the club does not run (2026-11-03). No cadence word here: the one cadence claim the site makes is the hero label, and it carries its source in src/content.json (D92). This sentence is also what a link unfurl shows, so it is written for a person. Re-read it when the venues or the paths change; `check:content` scans <meta content> for cadence words, so adding one means adding a source.
